recipes.name: Chicken Verde Sandwiches
ingredients_raw: 12 dashes hot sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Combine the frozen boneless chicken breast, prepared pizza sauce, and salsa verde in a slow cooker. Cover the cooker, and cook on Low 8 to 10 hours.

Use 2 forks to pull the chicken meat apart until completely shredded. Stir 1/2 cup sour cream into the chicken mixture. Place the chicken mixture onto the rolls. Top each sandwich with 1 ounce shredded Cheddar cheese, 1 ounce sour cream, and 2 dashes hot sauce to serve

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Verde Sandwiches
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breast cooks in a slow cooker with prepared pizza sauce and green salsa to make a tasty sandwich filling.

review.reviewBody: This was absolutely delicious!! Since one of the previous reviews stated that the chicken was a little bland, i added a packet of taco seasoning! This was perfect! The other thing i did differently was I shredded the chicken after 6-7 hrs and let it simmer for 1 extra hour so that it could absorb more of the flavors. This will be something I will be serving at home more often.

I changed slightly. I use 7 ounces mild Herdez Salsa Verde and 7 ounces of pizza sauce and cook for 3-4 hours on high in crock pot. My family loves this recipe. So easy! I’ve made it for parties and quick dinner during week with homemade coleslaw.

This was a great base but like others said it was a little bland. I added a pkg of taco seasoning, some hot salsa, the rest of a 14oz jar of the pizza sauce, a sliced onion, 2 cloves of garlic minced and some chicken broth... Much better.

I subbed in an equal amount of hot red salsa in place of the verde and it is still great. To serve, I put the cheese on the buns and heated up the chicken and made the sandwiches to put in a 350 degree oven to toast and melt the cheese. AMAZING!

I followed other reviewers' suggestions and added a packet of taco seasoning mix. I also used flour tortillas instead of the rolls. This recipe was a big hit in my family. I will definitely be making it again.

The whole family liked it -- including the picky kids! I thought it was slightly runny though so the bun was a bit soggy so I might dial back on the sauce next time or do a better job using a slotted spoon to dish it out. Will be making this again!

I wanted to keep the theme of "mexican" so I swapped out pizza sauce for enchilada sauce. I served these sandwiches with shredded lettuce. chopped tomato and the shredded cheese. The boys thought this was a great dinner! Great spin on our usual mexican themed dinner night.
This was a good cheap and easy recipe. It was not really good as a sandwich. I made some rice with black beans, tomatoes, and green onions and piled this on top and that was really good.

I really appreciated how easy this was AND that you can use frozen BLSL chicken! Mine was thawed because I hadn't read the recipe closely and only took about 4 hours to cook, on low. I used homemade pizza sauce ("Exquisite Pizza Sauce") from this site because it's what I had on hand. I'm not a big chicken fan and I was pleasantly surprised w/how delicious this SMELLED! However, the taste doesn't quite live up to the smell; you'll want to adjust accordingly w/your favorite additional seasonings (taco packet, Red Hot, chili powder, etc). This is a great jumping off point, just a tad bland, but that's easily fixed to make this an easy crock pot meal. THANKS for the recipe, FrackFamily5!

As written this recipe would be bland. I took the advice of others before me and added additional seasoning. Salt, onion and garlic powder, chili powder and cilantro, and added some red hot sauce into the mixture. You would think with all of the added seasoning it would be strong, but I still felt like it was missing something. I think I will attempt again but try the taco seasoning packet that another reviewer used. I believe this recipe has potential with the additional add ins.
Such a simple recipe and tastes so good. I used half the amount of chicken but kept the same amount of salsa and sauce. Sandwiches were messy but delicious!
It was good and easy to make no changes.

I added taco seasoning as mentioned by someone else. I felt this would be a great idea. This was just ok. My family hated it. I however added a whole bunch of chicken broth to it and made it into a soup rather than throw it out. Then it was good.
I needed easy and good tasting today. I also needed to use what I had in my pantry. This worked out great.

I made this exactly as recipe stated because I needed something quick to prepare and leave all day. We enjoyed over riced cauliflower one night and leftovers were made into enchiladas later that week. I will be making this again so we can use the shredded chicken for other recipes.

It was good but not worthy of 5 stars. My husband ate it and was surprised to learn it had pizza sauce in it. I was pleased that the pizza sauce took away the spiciness of the green salsa. I didn't use hot sauce because I have wimpy family. That probably would have made it worth 5 stars.
I added taco seasoning as well and really enjoyed the flavor. Only down side is it is VERY juicy and the bun gets real soggy real fast.
i really liked this recipe. it came out great
This is a keeper!! Followed the recipe and served with sautéed veggies! We have enough for sandwiches today! Yum!
